title: feat(service-automation)!: notify mails an email-field recipient, limited per address, and refuses a computed address no user holds
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-project-manager"} -->
_Requested by **Leehom** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01TenzsRopZj4jMbvjX8uz1X?thread=cmsg_01TenzsRopZj4jMbvjX8uz1X9qrU1uBiZrE9tU8kmzwSr1)_

Fixes #25571
Fixes #25647

Clause-②: no (narrowing: a recipient that the value expression of a `notify` node whose `channels` include `email` evaluates to an email address no user holds now fails the node at run time instead of being mailed)
Metadata-protocol: narrowed

## What changes

A `notify` node can now mail a person who is not a user. `recipients: { emailField: 'applicant_email' }` with `channels: 'email'` (the form PR #25645 declared in the spec, which until now failed the run at the node) mails the address in that `email`-typed field of the record that triggered the flow. Ruling 6377887204 (letter B): "recipient = a record field of type email only; templated; rate-limited per address; logged".

- **Where the address comes from.** `resolveEmailFieldAddress` in `packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/notify-node.ts` reads the field off the STORED trigger row by id (system context, projection `id` + the field), never off the `record` snapshot the run carries. Every way there is no address fails the node and says which: no trigger record, no data engine, a row that is not stored, an empty field, a value that is not one address. The failure names the field and the record, never the value, because a visitor typed it.
- **One address, nothing else.** The `email` field type's write check is `^[^\s@]+@[^\s@.]+(?:\.[^\s@.]+)+$` (`packages/objectql/src/validation/record-validator.ts`). It admits a local part holding a comma, semicolon, colon, angle brackets or quotes, and `role:x@y.z` reads as an audience selector to the messaging resolver. `isOneAddress` requires dot-separated RFC 5322 atoms and hostname labels, linear scans only. A list, a display name, a separator, a line break and an audience prefix each fail the node (pinned case by case). The grammar is plain ASCII on purpose: a non-ASCII character, a quoted local part or an IP-literal domain the email field type stored is refused, and the refusal says "does not hold one plain ASCII email address"; flows.mdx and the changeset declare it.
- **Templated and logged.** The address goes to `messaging.emit` as the audience with `channels: ['email']`. The existing chain does the rest: the recipient resolver keeps an address no user holds verbatim, the email channel sends a literal address as is, and the send is recorded as a `sys_notification` event plus a `sys_notification_delivery` row whose recipient is the address. Title and message render as for any notify. No messaging-side change was needed, so `packages/services/service-messaging/**` is untouched.
- **Rate-limited per address.** At most `EMAIL_FIELD_SENDS_PER_WINDOW` (5) sends per `EMAIL_FIELD_SEND_WINDOW_SECONDS` (1 hour) to one address, lowercased, across every flow. Measured first: service-messaging has no limiter. The repo's one fixed-window counter is `incrementFixedWindow` / `createLazyCounterStore` in `@objectstack/plugin-auth/rate-limit-storage`, counted in the kernel `cache` service and resolved at count time, which `@objectstack/service-sms` already uses. service-messaging cannot import it (plugin-auth depends on service-messaging, a cycle), so the limit lives in the node, which is also the only place that knows the address came from an email field. `@objectstack/plugin-auth` moves from a dev dependency to a dependency of service-automation (a new workspace edge, service-automation → plugin-auth; no cycle: neither plugin-auth nor service-messaging or rest depends on service-automation). A refused send fails the node before anything is written. A counter fault admits, said once at `warn`, matching the SMS quota's fail-open. The limit is declared best-effort in flows.mdx and the changeset.

## #25647, ruling 6386629237 letter B: a computed address must be a user's

Verbatim: "`notify` 收件人若由表达式（CEL 信封）求值得到一个不属于任何用户的邮箱地址，节点失败并给出定位提示指向 `{ emailField }`；求值得到某个用户的地址仍解析为该用户。元数据里**写死**的地址是作者常量，照常发出。"

- **Scope: nodes whose `channels` include `email`.** Only the email channel delivers to the raw address; a node on `inbox` alone (the messaging default) mails nobody, so its recipients pass to messaging unscreened, as before. Whether this reading of the ruling stands is put to the maintainer as a confirmation (open question 1 of the os-dev-report `6392322238`); the seat lands on it meanwhile, and screening every channel would be an additive follow-up.
- `resolveRecipients` now marks each recipient an envelope evaluated to that the messaging resolver would read as an address (the address the email channel would send to: a bare address, or the remainder after one `user:`, which the resolver hands on with no lookup; `role:` and `team:` yield user ids). `screenComputedAddresses` looks each one up the way the resolver does (`sys_user` by `email`, the id projected): a user holds it, the recipient becomes that user's id; no user holds it, the node fails, located (`recipients[0] evaluated to an email address — source: …`) and pointing to `recipients: { emailField: 'FIELD' }`. No data engine, or a failing lookup, fails the node: an address that could not be checked is not sent.
- `owner_of:` is not screened: its address comes from a stored owner field written through record writes, not from a string the expression builds (seat ruling on F1).
- A written-out address (`recipients: ['ops@example.com']`) never reaches the check and is sent as before (pinned).
- In-repo producers, re-checked per the card: `git grep -nE "recipients\s*:\s*\[?\s*\{\s*dialect" origin/main -- examples` at `47af3dd` gives 17 envelopes. The app-showcase ones over `record.owner` / `ownerId` do evaluate to addresses (that field holds the owner's email), but those nodes are `inbox` only, and no `notify` node in `examples/**` names the `email` channel, so no in-repo flow starts failing. HotCRM at `a4b3560`: 0 hits.

## Docs

`content/docs/automation/flows.mdx` gains the recipients paragraph PR #25645 left to this card: the email-field form with an example, what fails, the limit, the log, and the computed-versus-written-out rule.

## Left to #25696 (the spec card)

- The sentence "Delivery to an email-field recipient is not live yet: until the messaging service resolves the form, a run that reaches the node fails there." in the `recipients` describe of `packages/spec/src/automation/io-node-config.zod.ts` (and the generated `content/docs/references/automation/io-node-config.mdx` row) is now false and is #25696's to remove.
- Ruling B's describe half (name a written-out address as the author's constant; drop "an email address" from the audience-selector list) is #25696's.
- This PR does not touch `packages/spec/**` or `packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.ts`.

## Tests

New `packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/notify-email-field-recipient.integration.test.ts`, through the real `MessagingService` (outbox-backed), `NotificationDispatcher` and email channel:

- A: the stored address is mailed (a different address in the run's snapshot is ignored), the title renders, and the event row plus a `success` delivery row record it.
- B: eight values that are not one address each fail the node, write nothing, and the failure does not echo the value.
- C: no trigger record, a row not stored, an empty field.
- D: 5 sends admitted, the 6th to the same mailbox in other case refused with nothing written, another address unaffected.
- E1–E4: computed non-user address refused naming `{ emailField }`; computed user address resolves to the user id; written-out address sent as written; no data engine, computed address not sent.
- E5 (×2): an `inbox`-only node, and a node with no `channels`, pass a computed address to messaging unscreened. E6: `channels: ['inbox', 'email']` is screened.
- E7 (×2): a computed `user:ADDRESS` and `user:user:ADDRESS` no user holds under `channels: email` fail the node, nothing enqueued or mailed. E8: a computed `user:` plus a user's address resolves to that user.

Readings at `d4fd5968`: the file 23/23; service-automation 202/202 files (2,659 tests); example-showcase 39/39; plugin-approvals 96/96; `pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-automation typecheck` exit 0; eslint over the package exit 0; dogfood battery 295 files / 2,520 tests passed, 0 failed.

**Ablations** (each through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, mutation proven on disk, restored to the HEAD blob with `git diff HEAD` empty):

| Put back | Red |
|:--|:--|
| the limit check (`if (false)`) | D |
| `isOneAddress` (type check only) | B, 7 of 8 (the number value is still refused by the type check, so its pin stays green) |
| the computed-address screen (return recipients unscreened) | E1, E4 |
| the snapshot read (`context.record[field] ?? row[field]`) | A |
| the channel gate forced true | E5 ×2 |
| the channel gate forced false | E1, E4, E6 |
| the `user:` branch (old prefix refusal) | E7 ×2, E8 |

## Acceptance notes

- The limit is a constant, not a setting: 5 an hour covers the outcomes one applicant hears about several times over, and no producer asks for more.
- Gate sweep: the `dispatch-gates --commands` union at the final head, with every exit code, is in the os-dev-report comment on #25571; CI's check-runs are the authority for the full farm. `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `check:skill-examples` exit 0 after a full build (at `450832fb` and `d4fd5968`).
- A narrowing (`Metadata-protocol: narrowed`) owes one contract-review-tier review before the queue.
